tickets.title: File-private declarations: `private def` visible only in its own file (helpers)
tickets.body:
Problem: helpers (AoC's twice*/window* lemmas, the prelude's Text.splitCons/splitChars) join their namespace; only their own file should see them (Matt, 20 Oct 2026). There's no `private` today: docs/proposals/multi-file.md:498 ('Visibility of declarations: everything'), :1390 (later list), namespaces.md §8 table.

First step: a short design note (docs/proposals/), with the sketch: `private` before def/theorem/type; the name resolves only in its file; two files of one namespace may each have a private `helper` (the full name gets a file-unique part, as Lean does); bodies stay visible to the checker so a public function using a private helper still unfolds in other files' proofs (hides the name, not the definition; unlike Idris `export`); naming it from another file is E-PRIVATE 'private to file X'. Precedents: Lean private, Agda private blocks, Rust, Scala/TS. Design review gate applies.

Done when: the note is reviewed, then `private` is built with accept/reject examples (including the same private name in two files) and the AoC/prelude helpers are marked.

History: Matt, 20 Oct 2026.


Audit note (22 Nov): Audit 22 Nov: still true: no `private` keyword in crates/syntax; SW-2008 (commit 0f898a63f) added @[internal], which only hides helpers from listings (docs/proposals/private-helpers.md); real file-private declarations remain open.

tickets.title: Partial callbacks inside List.map run on native, --js and the reference runner, stack-safe
tickets.body:
The problem: A function marked {Partial} (it might run forever) can only be called from other partial code. `List.map` with a partial callback is not yet supported by the runners (native, `--js`, the reference evaluator), so a partial function cannot be mapped over a list. This is lane 3b of docs/proposals/partial-stage-3.md (section 7.4).

The change: make the three runners execute partial callbacks inside `map`, without growing the stack, and counting ticks exactly as the note specifies. The 4e generator gets partial callbacks through `map`.

What it should do: tick counts and traces agree across the runners; the 1M-element speed figures from the note are met; the `partial.rs` tick tests, `run_js`/`run_reference` on the new example and `effect_runtime` pass. Sonnet. Depends on 3a (library and elaborator part) being merged first.

Audit note (22 Nov): Depends on lane 3a of docs/proposals/partial-stage-3.md; verify 3a merged before scheduling. Family with SW-469 and SW-470 (3d, 3e), not duplicates. Audit 22 Nov: proposal says lane 3a built (and 3c merged, 8ce2c8b4d); 3b, 3d, 3e still to come (docs/proposals/partial-stage-3.md status line). No commit mentions SW-467.

The problem: calls to {Partial} functions are about 3x slower than ordinary ones natively and about 2x in JS; half of the native cost is the request node a partial call builds (D1182, docs/proposals/partial-stage-3.md section 5.4).

The change: runner fast paths plus a cheaper request node for partial calls, in both backends (D1182 A+B, lane 3d of the note, section 7.4).

What it should do: keep the change only if it gives at least 1.5x on `p2-collatz` (or the note's model comparison in `partial.rs`) with identical tick traces (D1219). If the gain is smaller, drop it and record the measurement on this ticket. Sonnet.

tickets.title: Effect.bindAssoc's proof uses Quot.sound: can it avoid it?
tickets.body:
The problem: `Effect.bindAssoc` (associativity of bind) is assumed as an axiom in std. Every theorem that uses it shows up in `stitchwort audit` with an axiom, and the roguelike had to restructure its code (draw first, then plan) to avoid needing a proved monad law under handlers (rogue PROOFS.md gap 2).

The change: prove it (probably needs a computation-equality/extensionality principle for Comp), or restrict it to the handler-free case.

What it should do: no axiom left in std for the effect monad laws; `audit` clean on the roguelike generation theorems. Related: SW-570 (symbolic stepping through handlers), SW-660.

Board audit (5 Nov 2026): Effect.bindAssoc is a proved theorem since SW-405; what remains is only its use of Quot.sound.

tickets.title: An unannotated lambda inside an {IO} body makes List.map/fold run at {IO} instead of pure
tickets.body:
The problem: in a `main : {IO} ...` body, a lambda without a type annotation passed to an effect-polymorphic List function (map, foldLeft) is given the {IO} row, not the empty row, so a pure fold in main pays effect dispatch (the interpreter builds effect nodes it does not need).

The change: when the lambda body performs no effects, infer the empty row for the lambda (docs/proposals/effect-polymorphic-list.md covers the design; unchecked whether this is already on its roadmap).

What it should do: a pure inline fold inside main costs the same as outside it; a test in the bench or a step-count example shows no effect dispatch. "For Matt": asks for his go-ahead on the inference rule.

Audit note (22 Nov): Asks Matt's go-ahead on the inference rule; no answer recorded. Audit 22 Nov: no commit or example mentions it; still asks Matt for the inference rule.

tickets.title: Proofs about effectful code run out of resources stepping through handlers symbolically (E-RESOURCE)
tickets.body:
The problem: when a theorem is about code that runs under a handler (for example the roguelike generator under `seeded`), the checker steps through the handler symbolically and hits E-RESOURCE. The roguelike therefore uses one `next()` per turn and derives every roll from an index hash (the "Dice" workaround, SW-571 text below), so its invariants are proved on the pure `resolve` function only.

The change: find out what the checker needs so effectful code can be proved as written (rogue PROOFS.md "Tried" section lists the attempts). Candidate pieces: Effect.bindAssoc without an axiom (SW-548), a lemma "seeded equals list handler", cheaper symbolic stepping.

What it should do: the generation theorems (generatedReachable, generatedFramed, newGameSound, drawn*) are proved over the free-style {Random} generator, and the roguelike goes back to calling `roll` freely, deleting the index-hashing.

Merged in from SW-564 (backlog review, 4 Nov 2026): prove those generation theorems over the free-style generator; blocked by symbolic handler stepping (E-RESOURCE) and the Effect.bindAssoc axiom (PROOFS.md gaps #2-3). Matt asked to revisit, 26 Oct.
Merged in from SW-571 (backlog review, 4 Nov 2026): per-turn Dice is a provability workaround: `step` calls `next()` once and derives every roll by index hashing (dice.upTo (3*index+1) ..., Dice.upTo = lcg(lcg(seed+index*7919)), Turn.sw/Random.sw) instead of calling `roll` freely. Then `seeded seed (step s c) = resolve dice s c` by rfl (Proofs/Step.sw), so all core invariants are proved about pure `resolve` for every seed. Revert to free `roll` once provable (D1305, Matt 26 Oct). Idea, untested: state invariants for any answers to `roll`, not via `seeded`.

Audit note (22 Nov): Audit 22 Nov: still true, the roguelike still uses the Dice index-hashing workaround (games/rogue/src/Rogue/Turn.sw, Random.sw, Proofs/Apart.sw).

The problem: with vm.overcommit_memory=2, `stitchwort run --native` reserves its full 64 GiB up front on the CLI thread and the OS refuses.

The change: size the reservation before the thread starts. That needs the JIT code and the terminal to be movable across threads (open item from NO6/NO7).

What it should do: `run --native` starts under mode 2 on a machine with ordinary memory, reserving only what the program needs, or giving a clear error naming the limit.

tickets.title: Consider D1428: Tail-resumptive clauses detected automatically, or marked like Koka's fun
tickets.body:
The compiler already detects them in state handlers; Effekt detects them too. Rec: automatically.

2 Nov 2026 (SW-1085, D2206): one more data point for declaring the mode. Osprey declares it per operation (a value operation, or `control` with abort/once/many resumptions; a handler can't change it), as Koka does with fun/ctl and Lexa does. A declaration would let the runtime take the in-place path without detection, and would give JS extraction the at-most-once guarantee it needs (DESIGN §16 Q9). `many` adds nothing here (every resumption is multi-shot already). SW-1087 (report/assert the fast path) addresses the silent-detection risk if detection stays.

From SW-792 (merged, backlog review 4 Nov 2026), D1429: if B goes ahead, limit in-place clauses to empty-row handlers at first. It avoids the subtle part Koka first got wrong, and still covers the parser's handler and every state loop. Rec: yes.

tickets.title: Postponable lambda kept from its in-place try can settle a shared type before an earlier postponed lambda is checked (argument-order dependence)
tickets.body:
From the SW-846 lane: in apply_args_postponing (check.rs), a postponable lambda that succeeds when tried in place is kept, so it can solve a metavariable (with the unfolded type) before an earlier postponed lambda is checked; the result depends on argument order (alias-functions.md §4). Check whether the remaining argument-order cases mostly come from this.

Investigated 29 Oct (night), no change. With def Counts: Type := List Nat, Counts.size, twice (f: b -> Nat) (g: b -> Nat) (z: b):
- A: twice (c => c.size) (c => List.length c) (Counts.of 1) rejected (misleading E-CANNOT-INFER from the first try);
- B: lambdas swapped, rejected (E-UNKNOWN-FIELD, c: List ?2) with no lambda postponed;
- C: both c.size, accepted; E1/E2: moving z first changes the inferred call type Counts vs List Nat.
Cause: whichever comparison solves b first decides its name; a later Counts never restores it (alias-functions.md place 3). SW-859's mechanism is one route into it; the §4/AoC cases are already fixed (SW-846) or not this mechanism.
Rules tried with a temporary switch: R1 (after one postponement, postpone all later postponable lambdas) accepts A, E2 but newly rejects examples/accept/lambda-postponed-alias.sw and a record-literal case; R2 (postpone all) accepts A, B, E2 but rejects lambda-postponed-alias.sw and twice (c => Int.abs c) (c => c) 3.
Options for Matt (lane's D1565/D1566): (a) leave, document with place 3; (b) R1; (c) R2; (d) retry with R1 then R2 only when the whole call fails (untested); and fold into a place-3 design (SW-858) where a later unification can restore the alias name. Lane recs: (d) if wanted before place 3, else (a); yes to folding into place 3. Repro files were in the session scratchpad (o/A.sw-F.sw).


30 Oct (orchestrator): folded into SW-817 (postponement queue). Its example, twice (c => c.size) (c => List.length c) (Counts.of 1), is the case the queue's scoped W1 keeps rejected today and that stage 5 (removing the lambda try-then-postpone in apply_args_postponing) is meant to settle; re-check after stage 5.


30 Oct (orchestrator, after stage 3 84e7e339): the lambda try-then-postpone counter is now 0 in accepted code; re-check this ticket's twice (c => c.size) (c => List.length c) (Counts.of 1) example after stage 5 removes the path.


D2085 (Matt, 31 Oct 2026): re-check on main after postponement stages 1-3 and 6; close if fixed, else fix.


31 Oct (D2085 lane): not fixed on main (02e83151). With `twice (f: b -> Nat) (g: b -> Nat) (z: b)`: A `twice (c => c.size) (c => List.length c) (Counts.of 1)` rejected, now E-UNKNOWN-FIELD with c: List Nat (no longer the misleading E-CANNOT-INFER); B (lambdas swapped) rejected, c: List ?2; C (both c.size) and z-first accepted. Cause unchanged: in A the second lambda, checked in place, solves b := List ?a from List.length's own parameter (not an unfolding), and the later Counts only fills ?a, so no place-3 naming rule can restore Counts; only not checking that lambda in place (stage 5, or R1/R2 above) or re-naming a solved meta would. Belongs to stage 5 of the queue; left open for it.

The generic-row map's recursive call sits in a continuation (bindIn e (f x) (y => Cons y (map xs f))), so TRMC doesn't apply (docs/core.md, after 'Tail calls as loops'); the limit is the 2,000,000-frame budget (crates/core/src/budget.rs, `frames: 2_000_000`, line 104 on 4 Nov), ~750 B/frame. Options for Matt: (a) close: the pure case was the AoC need (day 24's builders unconfirmed); (b) extend TRMC through effect continuations in interpreter and native (trmc.rs documents this as excluded for soundness); (c) std builders accumulate-and-reverse like partitionOnto (List.map is referenced 81x in List/Lemmas.sw, 43x in SortLemmas.sw, all would need re-proving); (d) raise Limits.frames for run (memory-bound, 3M frames ~2 GB) and/or a CLI flag. Lane recommendation: none given; orchestrator's: (a) unless a real program needs it.

Backlog review, 4 Nov 2026: SW-863 (done) fixed the pure case; this is the {IO}-callback case.

From SW-862 (29 Oct): value::conv (`pub fn conv`, crates/core/src/value.rs:2266 on 4 Nov) compares metas by number and never follows a solution, so elaborator values computed before a meta was solved compare unequal after. SW-862 added Ctx::conv_now (check.rs: conv, then refresh both and conv again if anything is solved) and used it in cases.rs. Sites left alone as harmless or contrived: cases.rs take_apart (587, 602), omega.rs:212 and 2008, ring.rs:927, data_auto.rs:209. Option A: make conv force solved metas at each step (kernel terms are zonked, so the code never runs in the kernel; fixes every elaborator call at once) at the soundness boundary. Option B: keep conv kernel-only and move elaborator sites to conv_now one at a time. Lane's D1545.

Backlog review, 4 Nov 2026: since the Globals split (step 8e) the evaluator takes `&Ev` with `&dyn Metas` (SW-1190), so the elaborator can now pass a meta view to the checker. That weakens the premise 'kernel terms are zonked, so the code never runs in the kernel'. Open question: is Option A now cheap?

tickets.title: Literature research: lessons (how NOT to run it) and where the partial results are; PAUSED
tickets.body:
PAUSED (Matt, 29 Oct 2026). Literature trawl SW-894 went badly. This ticket records how NOT to run it, and where the partial results are. Restart only on Matt's say-so.

== What went wrong (don't repeat) ==
1. Lanes couldn't read papers and nobody checked first. No PDF tool is installed (pdftotext, mutool, qpdf absent) and WebFetch can't read PDFs. Elaboration, proof automation and kernel registers were written largely from abstracts. Fix that works (tested): `nix shell nixpkgs#poppler-utils -c pdftotext paper.pdf -` (package name has a hyphen; `poppler_utils` is the old name and fails). Test the toolchain on a real paper BEFORE starting a lane.
2. Caveats were buried. Each lane listed "sources not reached / abstract only" at the END of its report; the orchestrator relayed the findings and rankings and dropped the caveat. Rule: every register and every report must START with counts: screened / carded / read in full / not read. Every card says "Full text: read (source)" or "NOT READ"; NOT READ supports no ranking or recommendation.
3. Unverified claims were relayed as fact. Lanes said "the session's web-search budget ran out"; the orchestrator first repeated it, then (after one successful search) wrongly said there was no budget, without checking the docs. The docs (code.claude.com/docs/en/tools-reference, "Session search limit"): an interactive session has 200 WebSearch calls shared with ALL subagents; at the limit searches silently do nothing; refills ~100/hour (v2.1.290+, CLAUDE_CODE_WEB_SEARCH_REFILLS_PER_HOUR); cap raisable via CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_WEB_SEARCHES_PER_SESSION; /clear resets. Seven parallel research lanes at ~30-40 searches each exhaust it. Plan the search budget; run at most one searching lane; lanes report immediately if searches start doing nothing.
4. Too many lanes at once (up to 4, plus helpers). Stopping a lane does NOT stop the reading helpers it spawned; they kept running and reporting after "stop". After stopping a lane, check ListAgents and stop its children.
5. Decision spam: each lane asked 2-3 decisions; the orchestrator listed them all. Keep to one or two decisions at a time.
6. Personal data: the orchestrator once sent Matt's email address to the Unpaywall API (one request, DOI 10.1145/3434341). Never send personal data to any service. Use Semantic Scholar's API (no email needed) for open-access lookups.
7. Leads can be wrong: the kernel redo's readers found the first kernel register misstated papers (Géran says nothing about Lean's level normaliser; the sort-polymorphism paper doesn't use "quality variables" and mechanises nothing; the definitional-inversion paper isn't about Lean with quotients; MetaCoq found one Coq kernel incompleteness, not a soundness bug). Re-derive claims from full texts, never from a previous register.
8. Access problems that remain: ACM DL returns 403 / HTML to scripts; HAL sometimes returns a bot page (check `file x.pdf`); TU Delft repository refused connections; image-only PDFs/slides can't be read (no OCR). Keep a "for Matt to fetch" table.

== Process to use next time ==
Before starting: test pdftotext on a real paper, check the WebSearch budget headroom, give the lane a reserved D-number range and the reading protocol (counts first, read in full or NOT READ, for-Matt-to-fetch table, no personal data). When it reports: verify its counts and a sample of cards against the files before relaying; lead with how much was read. Log progress as you go. Merge only after reading the diff and running the merge tier.

== Partial results and where they are ==
On main, docs/research/ (index README.md):
- inductives.md: RELIABLE. Screened 56, carded 21, read in full 19, not read 2 (counts line checked; cards state how read).
- infrastructure.md: RELIABLE for what it read (59/26/24/2), but its searching stopped when the shared search pool ran out; §9 lists what wasn't searched.
- kernel.md: UNRELIABLE (deep reads rest on abstracts; several claims shown wrong, see 7).
- elaboration.md: UNRELIABLE (many cards from abstracts).
- proof-automation.md: UNRELIABLE (most cards from abstracts).
- effects.md: UNVERIFIED (lane says it extracted PDF text itself; how much it really read is unknown).
Not merged:
- Compilation register, read in full (52/23/21/2): branch worktree-agent-aa5688f5b03448c33, commit 6257c83e (docs/research/compilation.md only). Counts and cards not yet independently checked by the orchestrator.
- Kernel redo (stopped): branch worktree-agent-a9e4342358a8087bb has NO commits. Its reading helpers finished full-text cards for 14 papers; those cards exist only in the subagent transcripts under ~/.claude/projects/-Users-matt-repos-mdr-stitchwort/3eef38f5-69c2-4f26-b1b3-39bd97dd0fd4/subagents/: agent-a6c7b1f49e6842134.jsonl (Pujet-Tabareau OTT POPL22, POPL23, TOPLAS25; Danielsson 2026), agent-a5b1ab6622a0e8038.jsonl (Bezem et al. universe polymorphism + GAT follow-up; Martin-Löf à la Coq; Lennon-Bertrand certified conversion), agent-ab9e6a590975a44f6.jsonl (Géran CSL26; Rosain et al. sort polymorphism POPL26; Sterbac-Sterling; Jiang-Hu), agent-a88141c03e0c28f43.jsonl (MetaCoq JACM; Definitional Inversion 2026). agent-a2e28c767a15a9987.jsonl (rewrite rules / SProp) was stopped mid-way.
- Downloaded PDFs and extracted text (29 papers, incl. the above, Lean4Lean TYPES25, Felicissimo LICS26, Taming of the Rew, Rewster, Pujet thesis) are in ~/stitchwort-papers/ (copied 30 Oct from the session scratchpad, D1975; outside the repo; 29 PDFs plus extracted text, 32 MB).
- Papers for Matt to fetch by hand: Escot & Cockx ICFP 2022 (10.1145/3547644); Ko, Chen & Lin ICFP 2022 (10.1145/3547629); Eris PLDI 2026; Sisyphus PLDI 2023 (10.1145/3591221); Lambda Set Specialization PLDI 2023 (10.1145/3591260); Verified Extraction Coq to OCaml PLDI 2024 (10.1145/3656379).
- Plan and clusters: SW-894. Session transcript: ~/.claude/projects/-Users-matt-repos-mdr-stitchwort/3eef38f5-69c2-4f26-b1b3-39bd97dd0fd4.jsonl.


Scope (Matt, 30 Oct 2026): the one-lane-at-a-time rule applied only to broad literature surveys (the SW-894 trawl), and is now deleted. Targeted research for a design question can run alongside other lanes. Everything else here still applies: full texts, counts first, NOT READ supports nothing, the paywall rule, no personal data, and planning the shared WebSearch budget when several searching lanes run.

tickets.title: Consider congruence closure in cases (D2000): first show it would simplify existing proofs
tickets.body:
From the proof-automation research register (docs/research/proof-automation.md §5.1, ticket T1, decision D2000), redone from full texts 30 Oct 2026.

Idea: a congruence-closure step inside `cases`, as in Lean 4's `grind` and every SMT solver, using only the facts already in scope. Equations in scope are grouped into classes of equal terms, closed under "equal arguments give equal results". Two different constructors in one class makes the branch impossible; both sides of the goal in one class proves it. Stage 2 would apply each local ∀ hypothesis once to the matching facts. Probes that fail on main today (register §5.1): (1) `xs = Cons 1 Nil` and `xs = Nil` both in scope; (2) `f a = c` from `a = b` and `f b = c`; (3) `(y: Nat) → lookup = Some y → y < 5` with `lookup = Some y0`, goal `y0 < 5`.

Assumptions of D2000 in full: (A1) comparing class members by their computed form, as `cases` compares atoms now, is enough, without full conversion inside the closure; (A2) the classes at one `cases` node are small (tens of terms), so the step costs little when it fails; (A3) congruence steps written with `J`, with `Bool.uniqueEq` or `DecEq.uniqueEq` equating proof arguments, type-check for the dependent calls the target proofs contain.

D2000 (Matt, 30 Oct 2026): NOT prioritised yet. First gather evidence that it would simplify EXISTING proofs. Before any design: survey std, examples, aoc and games/rogue proofs for steps that chain equations by hand (Eq.trans/Eq.sym/Eq.cong chains, rewrite sequences, matches that only exist to rule out a constructor clash, manual instantiation of a ∀ hypothesis) and that a congruence-closure step in `cases` would make unnecessary; count them, list file:line, and rewrite a few by hand-simulating the step to show the saving. Also cross-check against the cases follow-ups in SW-608. Prioritise only if the survey shows real savings.
30 Oct (survey lane): rebased, read §5.1/D2000, cases.rs closers, proving-guide; starting grep survey of std/examples/aoc/rogue.
30 Oct (survey lane): probes on main: cases fails p2 (even x = True, even x = False ⊢ Void), p3 (o = Some 3, o = None, Option var), p4/p8 injectivity via shared term, p6/p9/p11/p12/p14; passes Nat trans (omega) and h ⊢ h. Writing a leaf classifier for Eq.trans/sym/cong chains next.
30 Oct (survey lane): trial edits (reverted) replacing steps by today's cases: 8 already close (Day06 x5, Day24 settleMore, rogue Loop:24, Rules:24); 12 fail today (Day06 stepTurns, Day16 Moves x3, Day13 Cramer, rogue Loop:20, Day15 sameBox x2, Day17 comboUnique, Day23 x3). Hand-simulating CC on the failures next.
30 Oct (survey lane): 32 sites tried in situ (reverted): 16 already close with today's cases, 16 fail; hand-simulated CC closes 14 of the 16 (3 only with disequality, 1 only with stage 2), 2 unclear. Line savings ~0 per site. Writing docs/research/congruence-closure-evidence.md.

EVIDENCE (30 Oct, branch worktree-agent-a1fb65a24d4a7ede6, 99e85ba2, docs/research/congruence-closure-evidence.md): Congruence closure would close steps today's cases can't, but it saves almost no lines. Candidates (multi-step, all-local leaves; lenient classifier): (a) Eq chains 64 + 11 with And projections; (b) rewrite <locals> in rfl/<local>/at 88/22/19; (c) clash from 2+ local equations 63 (39 are one std Map/Set/Ord shape); (d) local ∀ instantiated 14; (e) helper lemmas 1 (rogue someNotNone, which today's cases already does). 32 sites tried in place (reverted): 16 already close with today's cases, 16 fail. Hand simulation of the 16: 6 close by stage 1 at the root, 4 at the first open case only, 3 only with disequalities, 1 only with stage 2, 2 unclear. Estimate: about 150 sites, about 0 lines each (each step becomes `cases` on the same line, about 30 chars); 4 lines saved in 21 sampled cases; about 10-30 lines across about 70k proof lines. Separately, 389 one-hypothesis clash arms are already closable by today's cases and were never converted. The friction notes have no complaint about chaining local equations; their Eq.trans uses are workarounds through library lemmas, which CC over local facts doesn't reach. Recommendation: DEFER. The evidence that sites exist is moderate (hand simulation, not an implementation). The evidence that line savings are negligible is strong. There is no evidence either way on ease of writing.

D2060 (Matt, 30 Oct 2026): DEFERRED to backlog. Evidence: docs/research/congruence-closure-evidence.md. If revisited, start with the narrower check: two local hypotheses `t = C1` and `t = C2` about the same term with different constructors close the branch (39 of about 75 chain sites), not full congruence closure.

Note (moved from the where field, board audit 5 Nov 2026): deferred (D2060); evidence in docs/research/congruence-closure-evidence.md

tickets.title: Error enumeration for soundness testing (D2031): one type mismatch at every check site, kernel first
tickets.body:
D2031 (infrastructure register C3, §5.1 "Error enumeration", T2), from the Eris paper (Sotiropoulos and Su, PLDI 2026, doi 10.1145/3808320, read in full). Matt, 30 Oct 2026: backlog for now.

Idea: from an accepted program, at every place the checker compares an expression with a known expected type, substitute one expression of an incompatible type (one change per variant); every variant is ill-typed by construction, so any acceptance is a soundness lead. Stage K (kernel, small): over kernel terms, at the check sites in crates/core/src/check.rs (arguments, ascriptions, constructor fields, let values, case branches, definition bodies); oracle: refused with E-TYPE-MISMATCH / E-UNIVERSE / E-REFL; out-of-budget variants dropped. Stage E (elaborator, tooling): source-level, using the hover record of expected types; coercions, postponed comparisons and numeral defaults count as compatible. Options: (a) random overwrites in the existing 400-case daily fuzz run; (b) error enumeration, kernel first, on demand (task fuzz:enum) with a small daily sample. Recommendation: (b), stage K first. Assumptions in full: infrastructure.md §8, D2031.


Audit note (22 Nov): 22 Nov 2026 audit: Still true: no error-enumeration oracle exists; Matt put it on the backlog (D2031).

tickets.title: match last resort: generalise at the end and re-check when only the match's own alternatives fix an unknown (step 4.0 follow-up)
tickets.body:
From SW-817 step 4.0 (D2095, 31 Oct 2026): a generalising match now waits while what it reads holds an unknown. If the only thing that would fix that unknown is the waiting match's own alternatives, it waits for ever and the program is rejected, e.g.
  let g := acc => match List.length [acc] with | Zero => 0 | Succ k => plus acc k
  n   -- g never applied
Main accepted this before step 4.0. Fix as Lean does as a last resort: at the end, generalise anyway, then re-check the choices (occurrence test, motive) once the alternatives have solved the unknown. See postponement.md "As built (step 4.0)". No corpus program has this shape.


Audit note (22 Nov): Audit 22 Nov: still true: examples/accept/match-waits-inferred-type.sw covers the waiting match but no last-resort generalise (no commit names SW-929).

tickets.title: Kernel: refine context types lazily at case splits (case cost O(cases x context) today; lifts SW-1053's 64-hypothesis cap); also count Int/char literal hypotheses toward the cap
tickets.body:
From SW-1053 (2 Nov 2026). The kernel refines the whole context at every case: check_num_case (crates/core/src/check.rs:1195 on 4 Nov, its `refined` closure at :1249-1254) runs substitute_in over the whole environment and every context type — a read-back and re-evaluation per entry — at each number; check_case (begins at :853) does the same per constructor. So a case split with many hypotheses in scope costs O(cases x context). This is why a catch-all equation after N number arms costs N^2 (SW-1053 capped it at 64).

Idea: record the pending substitution per branch (variable, value, environment) and apply it to an entry's type only when it is looked up (variable type lookup ~line 243; the matched variable's type ~870, ~1215; nested case refinement and the index unifier apply what's pending first). Entries that are just their own variable can be skipped outright (cheap and safe on its own). Effect: each arm of an equation proof touches only its hypothesis and the goal, so the cap could be lifted.

Cost/risk: trusted kernel. Must stay equivalent to eager refinement (eval(quote_folded(v)) gives the same value), keep checked terms and hashes (Term::Eq's filled-in type is read back from these types), and compose nested refinements in order. Skipping entries that don't mention the variable doesn't help here (every hypothesis mentions it).

Also from SW-1053: the 64 cap counts only Nat hypotheses — Int literal hypotheses aren't counted, and a big character table's merged notListed is one hypothesis with the same N^2 proof cost. Cover those with the cap (small) unless this kernel change lands first.

Backlog review, 4 Nov 2026: SW-1106 (done, 20f98102d 'a branch's refinement returns values that don't mention the matched variable as they are') already removed part of the cost. What remains: the per-entry read-back and re-evaluation for entries whose type does mention the variable; re-measure before building.

Audit note (22 Nov): Audit 22 Nov: still true: crates/core/src/check.rs:1642 `refined` still runs substitute_in over the whole context per case.

tickets.title: Report whether each handler runs as a fused loop and which clause stopped it (check --explain-handlers), then an attribute that fails when it doesn't (research T5, D2207)
tickets.body:
Step 1 result (Sonnet, 2 Nov 2026; under load 7-37, re-time before citing). SW-861's natural form is fused on the machine now (01462c09): Std.Parse Parse.next over 160,000 chars, natural vs pair form same user time (~4.6-4.8 s vs 4.55-4.64 s), natural 13% less memory (1.39 vs 1.60 GB); the 28 Oct 9.4 s / 2.2 s doesn't reproduce. Discriminator: at 1M operations a fused natural handler completes, an all-non-tail control hits the recursion limit (machine and --js). JS: fuse gets bodies=None so it can't follow a lifted %match; no slowdown seen in --js runs but not confirmed whether those ran on node. Memory grows ~5.8 KB per char in every form (fusion doesn't bound it). SW-738 revert: plausible after a JS check (build --js, big parse in node) and re-running the Parse.runFrom* rfl lemmas. Decline points in fusion.rs (11, each a silent Ok(None) or fallthrough today): partial foldComp; carrier not at the empty row / not state-passing; return clause not Done e; unrecognised handler structure; clause not x,k => ...; k used non-tail at <span>; depth > 200; > 64 matches followed; backend can't see inside match (JS); no arm of a match resumes; no clause resumes. Plus "partly fused" when one clause falls back. Plan: fuse returns Result<Result<Fused, Decline>> with a span; call sites ignore it; `stitchwort check --explain-handlers` calls fuse with the machine's bodies and with None, one line per handler (machine / js / not fused). Scratch: scratchpad/sw-1087/.

tickets.title: Audit vacuity check: false warnings; is random search viable? (option A done by SW-2765; B and C are SW-2767, SW-2769)
tickets.body:
From AoC 2020 day 4 (SW-1249, NOTES-2020.md item 6, ranked 2). The audit's vacuity check tries random inputs and warns when none satisfy a theorem's hypotheses. On day 4 all 8-11 warnings were false, all on compiler-generated equations (heightValid.eq.some with hypothesis value.stripSuffix "cm" = Some number; Spec.validValue.eq.if… with (key == "byr") = True): random texts never hit the literals. Same blindness: check --counterexamples missed a deliberately broken height range (between 151 193). Options raised: (A) skip generated equations in the vacuity check (they come from the definition, so can't be misstated); (B) seed generators with the definition's literals.

D2357 (Matt, 4 Nov): backlog only. Matt doubts random generation is a viable strategy for vacuity at all (hoping it finds inputs); revisit the approach itself (e.g. what a warning should require, or a non-random method) before doing A or B.

From SW-1210 (merged, backlog review 4 Nov 2026), option C: satisfy hypotheses of the form `f x = y` / `f x = Some y` in the counterexample search by computing y from the generated x, so audit tests 'if the program returns X' theorems instead of warning they may be vacuous. From aoc/NOTES-2020.md day 1 item 5: 6 of day 1's 16 theorems gave up this way. Medium, a day or two.
D2306 (Matt, 4 Nov 2026): backlog, consider later with evidence from other AoC days (2021/2024/2025 audits will have the same warnings).
Related, kept separate: SW-1063 (custom generators), SW-1247 (generator for non-equation proof fields).

7 Nov: option A only, as SW-2232 (D3231).

7 Nov: backlog, deprioritised. Matt, 7 Nov 2026: "let's deprioritize Stitchwort audit work. I think it's not obviously high priority. Keep it on the backlog."

Baseline, 8 Nov 2026 at a3d951195 (D3427 over-pace run, full audit:touched with search): Std 10 vacuity warnings (Float.Theory magUnitsNormal, magUnitsStepAcross, halveLow, firstLow, firstHigh, addInfComm; Parse linesBreak, linesBlank, lineBreakNotSpace, lineBreakChar); Aoc 126 (most in 2024 day 16 (16), 2021 day 18 (16), 2024 day 24 (15), 2021 day 16 (11), 2024 day 20 (10), 2020 day 4 (9)). 0 failures. Logs: orchestrator scratchpad audit-search-{std,aoc}.log.

Deep audit 8 Nov 2026 23:18 (main after SW-2439, SW-2445): 0 failures; vacuity warnings std 126, aoc 10, rogue 10 (146; this morning 136).


Audit note (22 Nov): 22 Nov 2026: option A is done (SW-2765, commit 3d3a13fed: no vacuity warning for generated declarations). Option B is SW-2767, option C is SW-2769. Matt's doubt (D2357) about random generation as the approach stands.

Lane (Opus, 9 Nov 22:56-23:06, est. 120 min): no bug found in Stitchwort's code; best lead is a Linux kernel bug. The crash path (CLI main -> host::stack::run_on thread -> LibraryIndex::build -> decl_refs -> names_and_proofs) is safe Rust over a freshly parsed, self-owning AST (ast::Name owns its String). The CLI has no other live thread then (main is in pthread_join; the other spawns in elab/core are test-only), and no native code has run yet. The only unsafe code or FFI on the path is host::stack (reviewed: sound, also under musl's TLS-on-supplied-stack), musl and mimalloc v3.3.2 (libmimalloc-sys 0.1.49 builds v3 by default).
Lead: Linux 7.0 to 7.1.8 and 7.2-rc1 to rc6 have a bug in page-table reclaim (CONFIG_PT_RECLAIM, def_bool y, used on MADV_DONTNEED): zap_pte_range flushes the wrong address when it frees an empty PTE table, so a CPU can keep a stale paging-structure-cache entry to a freed table. Writes get lost, pages read back as zero, pointers go bad, in a single thread too. It's worst on AMD (EFER.TCE) and on Intel with INVPCID and KPTI off. Introduced by 4c640eb4181c (v7.0); fixed by torvalds/linux 478a1c3abebf "mm: fix incorrect flush address in direct page table reclaim" (5 Aug 2026; in v7.2-rc7, v7.2, and stable v7.1.9 and later; v7.0.14 is still unfixed). Ref: BurntSushi/ripgrep#3494, the same symptoms in musl builds. mimalloc v3 purges freed memory with MADV_DONTNEED 1 s after it's freed (prim/unix/prim.c _mi_prim_decommit; purge_delay 1000), and LibraryIndex::build runs just after a second of parsing churn. That fits: no memory pressure needed, Linux only, never on Speedwell (macOS), wrong results as well as crashes.
To confirm on Overmind: uname -r; zcat /proc/config.gz | grep PT_RECLAIM; cat /sys/devices/system/cpu/vulnerabilities/meltdown; lscpu | grep 'Vendor ID'. If the kernel is in the affected range: as a diagnostic, rerun job 51's failing tests with MIMALLOC_PURGE_DELAY=-1 exported (stops mimalloc's MADV_DONTNEED). The fix is a kernel of 7.1.9 or later, 7.2 or later, or the 6.18 LTS (Matt's host config). No code change, no regression test (a kernel bug).

Orchestrator, 23:10: asked Overmind for uname/config/CPU (lane done in 10 min, no code change). Waiting on its answer before going further.

Overmind, 23:12: kernel 6.18.60 (before the 7.0 regression), CONFIG_PT_RECLAIM=y, Intel, PTI on. So the kernel lead is dead. Next (lanes mode, Opus): a Linux ASan build of the CLI and test binaries for job 51's failing set; or that set with mimalloc swapped for the system allocator, to see whether the crashes follow mimalloc. Parked overnight (orchestrator's call): the remaining causes are mimalloc, musl or the compiler, and that needs Overmind time we've given to the night checks.

tickets.title: [Opus] Conversion keeps ~1.6 KB per unfolded level of a decreasing-checked recursion (innerN 2^128: 3.3 GB before the 2M-frame E-RESOURCE); shrink what Unfolding retains, or unfold lazily (fuzz_elab 0x25a5 case 4273)
tickets.body:
Found by Overmind, fuzz_elab CASES=12000 seed 0x25a5, 10 Nov 2026. Input on Overmind: target/fuzz-elab/25a5-4273.sw. Est. 60 min.

Lane notes (Sonnet, 10 Nov 2026): not fixed; cause found, needs a decision or Opus. The check already stops with a clear E-RESOURCE ("recursed more deeply than allowed", 4 s) but only at the evaluator's 2,000,000-frame limit, with 3.3 GB resident. Path: `unify_step` -> `unfold_folded` -> `force_now` -> `value::run`: conversion unfolds `innerN 2^128` (a `decreasing` function, so a fuelled helper) to head normal form before comparing with `innerN 0`'s. Every level pushes a `Frame::Unfolded` (64 bytes) and keeps its `Unfolding` and the helper's per-level values alive: about 1.6 KB per frame (measured: `innerN 200000` succeeds in 3 s and 744 MB, linear in n). A structural recursion of the same shape (no `decreasing`) is cheap (200000 deep: 0.3 s, 147 MB), so the weight is the `decreasing` helper's per-level terms. Not the work limit (10^10 steps, never reached), not postponed problems or a cache, not SW-2467's pattern chain. The options (unlowering `Limits::frames` for elaboration-time conversion only; a bytes-based cap; making conversion unfold lazily one step; shrinking the per-level retention) change what elaboration accepts or touch crates/core, so they are not done here.
Diagnosis (Sonnet lane, 10 Nov): not the step budget; conversion (unify_step -> unfold_folded -> force_now -> value::run) unfolds innerN 2^128 to head normal form, one Frame::Unfolded per level, until the 2M-frame limit gives E-RESOURCE after 4 s and 3.3 GB. ~1.6 KB retained per level (frames are 64 bytes): the unfolding data and the decreasing helper's per-level values. Without decreasing the same recursion costs 147 MB at 200k. Ruled out: postponed problems, caches, SW-2467's chain, SW-2418. Moved to Opus: shrink the retention (crates/core Unfolding) or unfold lazily.

Lane notes (Opus, 10 Nov 2026, stopped early at the orchestrator's restart; no code committed): cause confirmed with a heap profile (malloc_history at 300,000 frames) and a frame census. Two `Frame::Unfolded` per level (`innerN.%go`, `innerN.%step`), so the 2M-frame limit is hit at 1M levels. The frames themselves are small (64 B + a 128 B `Unfolding` each). The bulk (~3 KB/level) is the proof chain: `%go`'s `%rec` passes `Nat.leTrans (Succ y) (m x) k p h`, which holds the previous level's `h`, so every level's proof stays reachable from the innermost environment however the frames go. Each link is a glued `leTrans` call (5-arg spine: Rc 192 B + spill to capacity 8, ~640 B; plus an `Unfolding`) and `p` = `Omega.prove` (6-arg spine, same cost) with its certificate's constructor values rebuilt each level (~880 B, mostly closed terms). Measured (release, --no-cache): 2^128 with decreasing 4.8 s / 3.31 GB; without decreasing 0.83 s / 466 MB (2M levels); 200,000 with decreasing 3.1 s / 744 MB, without 0.32 s / 147 MB. Shrinking alone can't reach the goal: boxing `Unfolding`'s kept value (tried, reverted) saved only 3% (3.22 GB); exact-size spines and sharing closed certificate parts might reach ~2 KB/level at best, against ~470 B needed. Eliding frames for unshared unfoldings would make the loop tail-recursive and run on to the 10^10-step budget with the chain still growing: worse. Lazy proof arguments still chain through environments (~800 B/level est.) and are a large kernel change. So reaching the goal needs either a memory cap on a check (option 3: changes what's accepted, so Matt's call, like the frame limit) or a `decreasing` encoding whose proof doesn't chain (changes hashes; none found). Next: write this up as docs/reviews/SW-2639-decreasing-memory.md with a D question (memory cap?), ~30 min. Instrumentation used (pause at a frame count, names of frames, system allocator for malloc_history) was not committed.
Paused 10 Nov for a session restart. Next: write docs/reviews/SW-2639-decreasing-memory.md (cause: decreasing proof chain via Nat.leTrans holds every level's h, ~3 KB/level; frames are small) with a D question on a per-check memory cap (Opus, ~30 min). Branch lane/SW-2639 deleted after merge (only the note).

Write-up (Opus, 10 Nov 2026, paper lane, ~10 min): docs/reviews/SW-2639-decreasing-memory.md. Found a non-chaining encoding: `f.%go`'s recursive call decides `Nat.leq (Succ (m y)) k` afresh and passes the match's `found` (rfl at run time); the old `h` and `p` appear only in the impossible branch. Kernel and runtimes unchanged, hashes of decreasing defs change. Hand-written model, 200,000 levels with an omega proof: chained 3.0 KB/level (671 MB), fresh check 0.86 KB/level (251 MB), time about the same (measured). Memory cap not recommended (bytes differ native vs wasm). D3474 (number to confirm): adopt the fresh-check encoding? [rec: yes, ordinary Opus lane]. Parked speed findings: argument lists spilled at capacity 8; closed omega certificate values rebuilt per level.
Write-up merged (10 Nov): docs/reviews/SW-2639-decreasing-memory.md. Recommends D3474: generated fuel helper decides Nat.leq (Succ (m y)) k afresh at each call (proof rfl), old proofs only in the impossible branch; model 3.0 -> 0.86 KB/level; kernel unchanged; hashes of decreasing defs change. tickets.title: Check cache: a cache directory copied with a project is trusted (its salt travels with it)
tickets.body:
Severity 2 (likely hole, unconfirmed), from SW-2659 (docs/reviews/SW-2659-kernel-soundness-audit.md, F1).

The problem: the salt that should stop 'a cache copied from elsewhere (a committed .stitchwort, a download)' (docs/proposals/check-cache.md §3.1) is read from check/header inside the cache directory (crates/driver/src/check_cache.rs:149-173), so a whole directory that arrives with a project fits. Entries are sealed with plain BLAKE3, no secret. Loaded entries go through admit_trusted_*, which skips type and termination checking. check, test and audit all read the cache by default (crates/cli/src/main.rs:1440-1451, 2690, 2727).

Confirmed: cp -Rp a checked project with its .stitchwort to another folder and check there; the std.* entries keep their modification times, so they were read from the copy, not rebuilt.
Not confirmed: a forged entry proving False (needs the encoder in crates/elab/src/cache/codec.rs).

Fix, one of: (a) seal each entry with a keyed hash whose key is per user and outside any project; (b) audit always checks in full, and check-cache.md says a cache directory is as trusted as the compiler. A trust decision: Matt's.
Also (SW-2672 G3, cache/mod.rs:2671-2688): after a replay, the entry's stated hashes are installed without being computed; later entries' dependency checks trust them. Fix: a mode, on in tests and audit, that recomputes and refuses a mismatch. Part of D3475.

Audit note (22 Nov): 22 Nov 2026 audit: Still true: crates/driver/src/check_cache.rs:14 still reads the salt from check/header inside the cache directory.

tickets.title: f.induct: transmissionBits (2021 Day16) and sumMagnitudes (Day18) get none and no recorded reason: the recursive call is only in a several-expression match's scrutinee, so the generator decides they aren't recursive; record a reason, and consider splitting several-expression lifted matches (SW-2868)
tickets.body:
Review (SW-2868): worse than a missing message: a recursive call in a lifted match's scrutinee is a real recursive call, so the user is told the function doesn't call itself (false) and the induction principle lacks a hypothesis.

Also consider a debug_assert that no Term::Def(f) call in a generated statement/proof has more than f's parameter count of arguments (catches the SW-2876 class).

tickets.title: [Opus] A proof search inside a lambda still runs before a later argument fixes its type (postponement rule 2): lambdaFirst in a let fails E-OMEGA (SW-963 item 2; SW-3429)
tickets.body:
From the SW-3429 retest (main binary, 15 Nov 2026). Postponement stage 7's rule 1 (proof searches last) landed and fixes `rflUnderHole` and both SW-971 shapes (omega-before-later.sw checks). Rule 2 (docs/proposals/postponement.md:3319-3327, case 4: a failed `rewrite`/`cases`/`omega` inside a lambda waits on any unsolved unknown) is still missing.

Repro: /private/tmp/claude-550/-Users-agent-repos-mdr-stitchwort/8230e28a-2fab-4832-920d-c5160adb7e00/scratchpad/sw3429/item3-lambda-before-later.sw (docs/proposals/postponement/stage7/lambda-before-later.sw with `Option.someInjective found` updated for the implicit-argument signature). The failing part:

```stitchwort
import Std (Eq, List, Nat, Option, Void)

def next (n: Nat): Option Nat := Some (n + 1)

theorem eachStep ∀ (f: Nat → Option Nat)
    (each: (x: Nat) → (y: Nat) → f x = Some y → x < y) (xs: List Nat)
    (ran: List.map xs f = List.map xs next) (x y: Nat)
    (h: f x = Some y):
    x < y :=
  each x y h

def lambdaFirst (xs: List Nat) (x y: Nat) (h: next x = Some y): Nat :=
  let fact := eachStep _ (a b found => rewrite <- Option.someInjective found in omega) xs rfl x y h
  0
```

`nice -n 19 target/release/stitchwort check FILE` gives `E-OMEGA: omega needs to know the goal ... the goal still has unknowns the compiler hasn't worked out` at the `omega`. Expected: it checks (as it does as a theorem's body, where the after-expected path retries): the lambda's proof search should wait for `_` (`f`), which `rfl` for `ran` fixes later.

Fix direction: rule 2 of the stage 7 design: a failed search (`rewrite`, `cases`, `omega`, `ring`) waits on any unsolved unknown, not only the queue's. Opus (elaborator).

tickets.title: [Opus] cases can't close 'x ≤ 8, so x is one of 0..8' (E-CASES-BUDGET), and a catch-all arm gives omega no bound (SW-954 item 1; SW-3429)
tickets.body:
From the SW-3429 retest (main binary, 15 Nov 2026). Both halves of SW-954 item 1 still fail; day 6's `oneTimer` still uses `Succ (Succ (… above))` (aoc/src/Aoc/Year2021/Day06/Proofs/Proofs.sw:97-117). SW-1550 and SW-3335 fixed neighbouring things (Int comparisons as atoms; catch-all facts for `byDecision`/`auto`).

Repro: /private/tmp/claude-550/-Users-agent-repos-mdr-stitchwort/8230e28a-2fab-4832-920d-c5160adb7e00/scratchpad/sw3429/item4.sw

```stitchwort
import Std (Bool, Nat)

theorem oneTimerCases ∀ (x: Nat) (bounded: x ≤ 8):
    Bool.toNat (x == 0) + Bool.toNat (x == 1) + Bool.toNat (x == 2) + Bool.toNat (x == 3)
      + Bool.toNat (x == 4) + Bool.toNat (x == 5) + Bool.toNat (x == 6) + Bool.toNat (x == 7)
      + Bool.toNat (x == 8) = 1 :=
  cases

theorem oneTimerWild ∀ (x: Nat) (bounded: x ≤ 8):
    Bool.toNat (x == 0) + Bool.toNat (x == 1) + Bool.toNat (x == 2) + Bool.toNat (x == 3)
      + Bool.toNat (x == 4) + Bool.toNat (x == 5) + Bool.toNat (x == 6) + Bool.toNat (x == 7)
      + Bool.toNat (x == 8) = 1 :=
  match x with
    | 0 => rfl
    | 1 => rfl
    | 2 => rfl
    | 3 => rfl
    | 4 => rfl
    | 5 => rfl
    | 6 => rfl
    | 7 => rfl
    | 8 => rfl
    | _ => omega
```

- `oneTimerCases`: `E-CASES-BUDGET`, "it split on 9: `(x.decEq 0).holds`, `x.equal 1`, …"; the first open case has `x.equal 3 = True, x.equal 4 = True, …` together (two `Yes` splits that exclude each other). Fix: after a `Yes` split of `x.decEq k` substitute `x = k`, so the later splits compute (or give `cases` the congruence step of SW-904).
- `oneTimerWild`: `E-OMEGA`, "facts: `x ≤ 8` (bounded)", model `x = 0`. The `_` arm's `x ≠ 0 … x ≠ 8` marks (SW-3335) aren't visible to `omega`, as docs/syntax.md says ("the facts aren't hypotheses with names"). A smaller repro: /private/tmp/claude-550/-Users-agent-repos-mdr-stitchwort/8230e28a-2fab-4832-920d-c5160adb7e00/scratchpad/sw3429/item4c.sw (`wildOmega` fails; `wildLet`, which adds `let n0: x ≠ 0 := byDecision` per literal, checks). Fix: have `omega` read the arm's catch-all marks as facts (`x ≠ k`), so the wildcard needs no `Succ`×9 pattern or `byDecision` lets.

[Opus] Debug-build panic in hash_stability::examples: debug_assert at crates/core/src/value.rs:3515 'variable at level … read back with … in scope' (found by SW-3582 in a debug run; release builds skip it). Find the example, the cause, and whether release builds compute something wrong there
tickets.body:
Lane notes (27 Nov, Opus, ~25 min, est. 60): no longer reproduces at main 84e0ac68b (hash_stability::examples, all 785 examples, release with the assert made a plain assert!: passes). Cause found: the SW-3582 debug run predated SW-3592's fix 4366706f2, where Shown::unknown printed an unsolved instance's type with no names in scope (quote at level 0 of a value mentioning level 0). Putting `&[]` back reproduces it in examples/accept/rewrite-waits-for-dictionary.sw and map-set.sw (rewrite's nothing-found message, via pretty::value). In release the wrapped index printed as another name (`Add _`, `DecEq _k`) in messages a tactic retry discarded; no hash changed. Display only; the kernel rejects an out-of-scope Var (check.rs, E-MALFORMED) and eval's env indexing panics on one. Fix a3e7647ce: the assertion runs in release builds too, with a should_panic test that failed before it. Follow-up candidate: reference.rs:1049 reads back `level - 1 - l` unchecked the same way.

Cause: SW-3592 (4366706f2, 16 Nov 15:04) already fixed it; SW-3582's debug run was on an older tree. Reproduced by re-breaking Shown::unknown (names -> &[]): fires in examples/accept/rewrite-waits-for-dictionary.sw and map-set.sw. Release effect, measured: a wrong variable name (Add _, DecEq _k) in messages a tactic retry discarded; no hash changed, nothing reached the kernel. Change: the read-back level check is an assert in release too (E-INTERNAL via catch_unwind); test kernel::a_variable_outside_the_context_does_not_read_back. No Fable review: orchestrator's call, a debug check promoted to release, no kernel rule changed. Follow-up SW-4916 (reference.rs, arm_display.rs). Verifier: kernel::, soundness set and hash_stability::examples on all examples (EXAMPLES=.sw), 102 passed. Model result: opus, worked, 22 min (est. 60).

REOPENED (27 Nov, reverted in e7d31cc5f): with the check as an assert in release, `stitchwort check --no-cache Fmt.ReadBackFile` in tools/fmt panics: "variable at level 72 read back with 8 in scope" at value.rs:5333 (rc 101, an uncaught panic in a worker thread, not E-INTERNAL as the lane expected). So a caller still quotes outside its context on today's main, in release silently. Redo: find the caller with this reproducer, decide what release computes there (wrong name only, or a wrong term/statement), fix the cause, then re-land the release assert (a3e7647ce) with the fix.

Round two (27 Nov, Opus, ~17 min, est. 60): caller found. facts::is_fact judged `∀ x, C x` by applying the body to Value::var(level + 64) and, for a conclusion only the kernel judges (a def stuck on x: `Joins (Follows kinds) doc …` in Fmt.ReadBackFile's refusalNone, `Small x`), called cases::is_proposition, which quoted it in the context without the binder (backtrace: Search::add → is_fact ×5 → is_proposition → quote_folded → visit). Release effect, measured with an instrumented build: the wrapped index made the kernel refuse the term, so is_proposition's fallback answered true; all 10 hits in Fmt.ReadBackFile were Prop conclusions (right answer by accident), but `f: (x: Nat) → Fam x` (data) was also taken for a fact. byFacts applies facts only to Prop goals and the kernel re-checks proofs: nothing wrong proved, no example hash changed (hash_stability::examples, all examples). Fix: binders get levels from the context's end; a conclusion mentioning them is judged by the whole type's sort (Prop impredicative). Test examples/accept/facts-premise-under-binders.sw (panics before the fix). Release assert re-landed. `check` still reports such a panic as an uncaught worker panic (rc 101), not E-INTERNAL: by design in driver/parallel.rs (re-raised).

Round 2: caller was facts::is_fact (byFacts), applying ∀ bodies to Value::var(level + 64) and reading a stuck conclusion back outside its context (theorem refusalNone in tools/fmt Fmt.ReadBackFile). Release effect, measured: wrapped index, kernel refused the term, is_proposition then defaulted to \"proposition\", so is_fact said \"fact\" (right by accident in ReadBackFile; wrong for a data family probe). Only affects which hypotheses byFacts collects; no hash changed. Fix: binders get consecutive levels; a conclusion mentioning them is judged by the whole ∀ type's sort. Release assert re-landed. Example facts-premise-under-binders (panics before). Whole-project check --no-cache of tools/fmt (150 ns), aoc (291), rogue (3) clean before merging; verifier kernel::, soundness, accepted examples, hash_stability::examples 103 passed. Findings SW-4918 (worker panic exits 101), SW-4919. Model result: opus, worked (round 1 wrong: missed the live caller), 17 min (est. 60).

tickets.title: [Sonnet] Proving guide: proving a Parse program's reads: Parse.RunsFrom vs Parse.Runs, the runsFromMark + fOn split (a let matching Parse.mark().rest blocks it), literal-arm order matching the code for one-line per-kind proofs (SW-3965 findings); and fix the S1 sketch's std-theorem column where Pairs/printedJoins are the toy's
tickets.body:
Also (SW-3963): a full cases blew the 64-case budget on an if over a list; pull the Bool out as a parameter (pickItems).

Also (SW-3967): proving guide: a Bool test (a && b && c) = True reads as nested ∧ (use Both / let-tuples); an effect inside a constructor argument nests binds on the left so givesThen can't peel them (bind it in a let); a guard in a theorem's match doesn't refine; when to use givesThen vs ReadsAt (a peek coupled to a bump needs ReadsAt).

Also (SW-3970): state lemmas about named functions and pass facts as parameters; Doc.concat of stuck parts blocks rewrite (join with concatCong); a match can rewrite the goal before a later rewrite of the same Bool.

Also (SW-3968): split parser code so each function does one bind; lazy &&/|| over effects appears as if in the goal (write f (effect1) (effect2) with a pure f); higher-order inference needs [p := ...] hints; Parse.run needs let x := p(); x for lemmas to apply; check Syntax does not include sub-namespaces such as Syntax.ParseWalk.

Also (SW-3969): a match with an unreachable arm discharges an if whose Bool rewrite can't replace (E-REWRITE-MOTIVE); 'at' can't be a variable in a theorem (rewrite ... at), and the parse error points elsewhere (worth a diagnostics ticket).

Also (SW-4000): Some (x, effect) desugars to a nested bind, so givesDone needs [holds := ...] [x := ...] hints or a split parser (8 min).

Also (SW-3971): a match refining a hypothesis doesn't refine explicit arguments written in the arm (use a helper theorem over a variable); implicit list arguments through Doc.concat's inner match must be written out; run stitchwort fmt just before commit, not before scripted edits.

Also (SW-4004): bind associativity doesn't compute once stuck, so nest runsMap to follow the source's lets; runsBind/runsLook need the continuation written out after a peek or at (~10 times); lanes check their diff with git diff main...HEAD (three dots).

Also (SW-4006): which hole form prints goals (?name mostly gave unknown name; one hole at a time worked, 5 min); name Bool guards used in matches as a def, since a match doesn't replace a guard spelled with == or a projection (15 min).

Also (SW-4011): rewrite takes only proofs, not a definition's name (unfold by computing or a let with the computed type; 10 min).

Also (SW-4008): an effect inside a let value or tuple destructure is fine for the walk; only effects in if conditions, lazy &&/|| and match guards need splitting (10 min of needless splits); import Fmt (..) can collide with Syntax names (plainPattern).

Also (SW-4009): [a, ..effectful()] elaborates as nested binds, so let-bind the effect first; a match on Tok checks 81 cases (one hit 250M steps), prefer == guards; run fmt on touched files then git add before committing (the hook refuses).

Also (SW-4013): write witness theorems for lemmas with narrow hypotheses so the audit doesn't warn of vacuity.

Also (SW-4010): parenthesise rewrite inside tuples ((a, rewrite same, b) reads 'same, b' as rules; 5 min); test is a keyword, not an equation name; don't pipe git commit through tail, the hook's refusal is hidden.

Also (SW-4027): a nested match over ~20 cases elaborates exponentially (split it into runs); a check that hits timeout exits 0 with no output, which reads as a pass; a named match equation already rewrites hypotheses in scope.

Also (SW-4019): in statements write (x == y) = False, not (x != y) = True; a def over a type is : Type, not Prop; Parse.readsAtThen's continuation argument order needs a doc example.

Also (SW-4022): a match on a term that appears in hypotheses silently refines them, so later lemma calls naming it fail; split into helper lemmas with explicit hypotheses.

Also (SW-4020): import a clashing name explicitly (import Syntax.ParseCarries (Carried)); checks are cached by content (first check slow, later ~1 s).

Also (SW-4021): proving over a tuple-let over a stuck if (state a lemma about the stuck if/tuple, let _ fill the rest); && and ++ are right-associative.

Also (SW-4025): stitchwort run refuses while any theorem in the namespace fails and prints every open goal first; a note on probing (or a --quiet-goals flag, SW-3988).

Also (SW-4034): run check under timeout 240 when a mismatch may make it unfold for minutes.

Also (SW-4024): when two ReadsAt types differ at runPure/foldComp, run goal --at and give [p := ...] as the program writes it (15 min lost); Fmt's Unit shadows Std.Unit under import Fmt (..).

Also (SW-4039): where probe namespaces go, and that a clean check prints nothing that shows it ran; annotate numeric literals in unannotated let ... if (stays _ and rewrite misses).

Also (SW-4048): Lays/Puts ignore modes; a reading of blank lines through them needs the blank's break forced visibly (worth a line in Lays.sw's header).

Also (SW-4056): common spellings near the top: then is reserved (no .then method), rewrite h at name (not in), Eq .flipped (not .symm).

Also (SW-4049): x && True is stuck on x; after match on Bools byComputing finishes; Doc.concat needs concatTell; an index of the solid-text lemmas (solidSpaces, wordFilled).

Also (SW-4043): stitchwort goal takes a namespace (without one it runs the whole project); run needs main(): {IO} ().

Also (SW-4040): bind the hypothesis with let before a match that refines it, and use _ for arguments inside the arm (10 min).

Also (SW-4050): Prop defs with overlapping clauses stay stuck on a variable; put the catch-all last and earlier clauses constructor-complete; a how-to-patch-a-big-file note (Edit needs unique strings).

Also (SW-4062): there is no audit --std; audit std lemmas by full name (or --std-dir).

Also (SW-4061): develop lemmas in a scratch module importing only small modules (big imports re-check for minutes); after an && chain, confirm the edit landed; ascribe ((x != y): Bool) where a Bool is meant.

Also (SW-4066): std checks read from source with check --std-dir / STITCHWORT_STD_DIR (no rebuild needed except the hash test); audit a list of std names via xargs (zsh doesn't word-split $names); FileLexProofs.sw:296 W-REWRITE-THEN-COMPUTING one-line fixup.

Also (SW-4051): git grep -n -A N 'pattern' -- '*.sw' for .sw searches; stitchwort goal takes no namespace.

Also (SW-4057): briefs should give tools/fmt/src/ once, and say ../../target/release/stitchwort is the worktree's own binary (build if missing).

Also (SW-4031): the dev shell's sed is GNU (sed -i, not sed -i ''); size read-back lanes one step each.

Also (SW-4068): a dotted name (Note.unreturned) can't go in an import list; import the module.

Also (SW-4074): a comment on BlockAt saying its LineKind quantifier is inhabited (fullAnyLine) and read once (Parser.sw:678); briefs: walk records are type ...Of constructors (outsideOf, frameOf, ladderOf); std is crates/elab/src/std.

Also (SW-4070): eval needs a project file arg, join lets with ;, annotate Decl; compute expensive data once and write it out with one byComputing equation; brief pre-check for existing facts before scoping.

Also (SW-4078): board history command or timestamps on tickets; put the scope paragraph in a new ticket's body; say whether a worktree's check cache is warm.

Also (SW-4069): format every touched file before commit; keep a known-broken-namespaces note so lanes don't spend time checking the base.

Also (SW-4058): methods can't be imported by name (use (..)); HearProofs/StandsProofs checks take 1-2 min, run them in the background.

Also (SW-4075), proving guide: a record update's field doesn't compute through a match closing over the whole record (write helpers over the fields, as edgeOf); trueOrFalse plus an equation-taking helper avoids refinement mismatches.

Also (SW-4079): methods can't be imported by name (syntax.md import section); board show --body; NOTES: where driver-level tests live (import cycle Syntax.*Proofs <-> Fmt).

Also (SW-4071): proving guide: generalise with equations instead of big rewrites (E-RESOURCE); briefs: say when a named item isn't on the lane's branch yet.

Also (SW-4087): stitchwort search checks the whole project (grep crates/elab/src/std for names); proving guide: a tuple-let step, prove a plain-if copy equal first.

Also (SW-4076): give Doc.concat's list explicitly to *Concat lemmas; print start and stop time together at each date check.

Also (SW-4041): match a record on its plain pattern with a within hypothesis rather than destructuring all fields; don't rewrite over a computed printed1 of a literal tree (state the split, calc); a file-to-namespace map (MeaningProofs declares Fmt.Proofs).

Also (SW-4090): proving guide: pass a mutual member as a hypothesis (a def naming its type) and fill it with a lambda at the call site, to keep a big ∃ out of a mutual block; how check caching works for imported modules.

Also (SW-4086): check takes a namespace, not a file path; briefs: std sources are crates/elab/src/std (List lemmas mapMap, mapAppend).

Also (SW-4088): run formatWithin1 ad hoc with stitchwort eval tools/fmt/src/Fmt/Tests/Driver1.sw 'formatWithin1 "..."' from tools/fmt; scope open-goal tickets before estimating.

Also (SW-4089): briefs for goals: check whether the statement needs within1 (slice-1-only predicates end | _ => False); proving guide: && and ++ associativity; first check under StandsProofs/SettleOutputProofs takes ~2 min, run it in the background.

Also (SW-4099): proving guide E-REWRITE: rewrite with an equation whose left side the goal already computed past applies nothing silently; use a transport lemma.

Also (SW-4107): proving guide perf: pass explicit arguments to cancellation lemmas (appendCancel _ _ _ _ unified against a big equation ran 2e9 steps); rewrite at h fails once h has partly computed, use Eq.cong; briefs: say where a part's definitions may live (import cycles).

Also (SW-4077): stitchwort goal takes no namespace (use check NS for one namespace's goals); E-RESOURCE bisection tip.

Also (SW-4110): E-RESOURCE on destructuring printedTokens1 for a concrete Definition: keep decl abstract until after; E-MATCH-MOTIVE 'one scrutinee is part of another' example; and OneLineParts' doc for closersBareOneLine1 still says closersBareOfStands is open (fix after SW-4109).

Also (SW-4109): proving guide: && is right-associative (rewrite Bool.andFalse); Doc.Proofs.closesText (Prop) vs the Bool one under (..); a documented 'errors only' vs 'goals too' check one-liner.

tickets.body:
Progress (Sonnet lane, 20 Nov): pair kept, no code change. Cause (strong evidence, not a trace): with the pair dropped, followsThen's j/k are solved structurally from the False goal. That goal is the bare unfolded suffixes (mark().left + 1) ..., whose FIRST effect is the inner left() mark of suffixCalled, so ?j (mark()) := the continuation after that inner mark (y => unitCall y.rest ...), not the outer here.left+1 mark. j here then reads here.rest where the found side has state.at.rest. Closed needle mark() is refused by solve_abstracting (needle needs a variable the meta can't mention), so the abstracting fallback cannot correct it. True branch passes because the goal is Section (...), not Call-headed. Tried: pair dropped; only k dropped (twin side fails identically: hereTwin vs other.at); match moved inside/outside followsThen; branch order swapped: False fails every time. A model of the shape (examples-style, 2 marks) did not reproduce, so the exact trigger is some more detail of the real suffixes chain. Candidate elaborator rule, Opus review needed: for ?j (?p ()) with closed call needle, prefer abstracting occurrences of the needle in the goal over the first-order split when the goal's head call is the needle but occurs also as an argument.


Orchestrator, 20 Nov: parked behind the walk. Cause found (the first-effect split picks the inner left() mark in the False branch; the abstracting fallback refuses a closed needle like mark()); fix would be a closed-needle rule in the unifier. The walk (W1, SW-4239) reads each step off the body itself, so it should make this pair unnecessary; decide after W1 with SW-4355 and SW-4363.
Model result: Sonnet, worked (diagnosed; correctly stopped before a unifier change), 15 min (est. 35)

Lane (Opus, 26 Nov): natively quadratic too. Release CLI (64 MiB stack): 1,000 levels 141 ms elab, 2,000 582 ms, 4,000 2,392 ms, 8,000 E-RESOURCE (nested too deeply; the 64 MiB stack reaches about 6,000). Steps linear (13 a level); Budget visits quadratic: f at depths 100/200/400/800 = 6,292 / 22,542 / 85,042 / 330,042 (about n²/2), same for a polymorphic head. Cause: check_special (check.rs, the may_perform_at call before checking a plain value) asks effects::may_perform_at of every expression checked, and that walks the whole argument chain through call_performs; each level of the nesting asks again of its own argument, so n levels walk n²/2 nodes. sample of 5,500 levels: about 98% of busy samples in call_performs, Expr::span, Registry::is_def, scope lookups. Times 1,000/2,000/4,000 levels: 141/582/2,392 ms, steps linear; visits ~n²/2. Cause: effects::call_performs per level. No fix (memo safety unclear); design SW-4889. Model result: opus, worked (report, no fix), 8 min (est. 50).

tickets.title: fmt: a comment inside empty brackets that start an or-pattern is moved after them, splitting the pattern so the output doesn't parse (fmt refuses)
tickets.body:
[DeepSeek] Found by Overmind, fuzz batch 23 (`task fuzz:fmt SEED=0x26112617 CASES=1000000 COMMENTS=0.3` at 98f88b21a, case 59013). Internal error: "the output doesn't parse: expected `=>`, but found `|`". Fails safe: fmt refuses (rc=2) and leaves the file unchanged. Unrelated to SW-4853.

Repro: docs/reviews/repros/fuzz-fmt-26112617-59013.sw (checks fine with the CLI).

Cause (Overmind): the formatter moves a comment inside empty brackets to after them, `[-- c⏎]` → `[] -- c`. As the first alternative of an or-pattern, the comment's line break splits `[]` from `| [_, .._] => 0`, and a `|` continuing the pattern on a new line there is an E-PARSE. Harmless when `=>` follows the brackets, or for a plain `[-- c⏎]` value.

Fix: place the comment so the output re-parses (e.g. keep it inside the brackets, or put the or-pattern's continuation where the parser takes it), in crates/fmt; check the self-hosted formatter (tools/fmt) for the same placement and match it (formatters stay in sync). Add the repro as a fmt test, failing first.

Fix: in an or-pattern, a comment before the closer that ends an alternative followed by `|` stays inside the brackets (the closer starts a line), so the next `|` stays on the closer's line. Golden or-pattern-bracket-comment (failed before; covers the repro, a non-empty bracket, and unchanged `=>` and plain-value layouts). Layout for this rare input is vertical but parses and is idempotent. fuzz:fmt 20k COMMENTS=0.3 at the seed clean. tools/fmt refuses the input (outside slice 6a), so the formatters agree. Model result: deepseek, worked, 17 min (est. 25).

tickets.body:

On the public playground (released today, SW-4923). tickets.title: stitchwort search: no way to leave abilities open: {_} is refused and {e} doesn't match {Parse Char}; make an ability hole match any row
tickets.body:
[Opus] Matt, 27 Nov 2026: "Is there a way to search for something where you're not quite sure what abilities might be involved?" Tried by the orchestrator, release CLI at main, `search --in Std`:
- `() → {_} Int`: E-ABILITY "expected an ability" (Matt's try).
- `() → _ Int`: E-NOT-A-TYPE (Matt's try).
- `() → {e} Int` and `() → {?e} Int`: elaborate, but the only result is Std.Effect.bindIn (relaxed pass, with the "weaker" warning); Std.Parse.int, `() → {Parse Char} Int`, is not found: the row hole doesn't match a concrete row.
- `() → {Parse _} Int`: finds Parse.int (works when the ability is known).
Wanted: a way to leave the abilities open that finds every `() → {…} Int`: `{_}` (and a named `{?e}`/`{e}`) accepted as "any row" in a search pattern, matching any row including the empty one; possibly a pattern with no braces also matching computations with abilities (decide, and say). docs/syntax.md's search section and the guide get the syntax. Run after SW-4935 (search speed), which works in the same code.

Matt, 27 Nov: design first ("designing how we write search for things with abilities that we're not sure of"). A paper lane writes a note in docs/proposals/: the syntax for an open or partly known row in a search pattern ({_}, {?e}, {Parse, _}, no braces meaning any?), how it matches (rows as sets, empty row, order, a row variable in the candidate), how it ranks, error messages for the old spellings, what Lean/Koka/Unison/Hoogle do for effects or type classes in search (verified and cited); options with a recommendation; decisions for Matt listed. tickets.title: worktree:new builds the release CLI up front: 4 min 17 s at 22:13 on 27 Nov after a crates/core merge with two builds running; consider letting the lane build on first need
tickets.body:
[Sonnet] Matt asked why making worktrees was slow (27 Nov). kache makes it seconds when another checkout built the same code; after a core merge nothing is cached.
More evidence (27 Nov 22:27-22:30): worktree:new SW-4953 real 138 s (user 337 s), then scratch:new sw-4946 real 152 s (user 358 s), from the same main with no compiler change between them (only a docs merge): the second should have been kache hits in seconds, so kache looks to be missing, not just cold. Investigate first: kache hit/miss stats for those two builds (kache stats or its log), whether the paths or env in the cargo config differ between worktrees and scratch clones, and the stale-artifact switches. Reproduce: two worktree:new runs back to back on an unchanged main, timed.

Cause: stitchwort_elab's std_dir.rs baked env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR") (absolute path; kache keys it unremapped: 'kept absolute: CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR is never path-only'), so elab missed in every checkout and driver, lsp, cli missed with it (extern hash). Dependencies and core/syntax/rt hit. Fix f6df4fb91: the executable passes the build tree (set_build_tree). Same-commit fresh worktree build: 106 s -> 20 s; kache:check ok. Remaining ~13 s: the final bin is an adaptive-incremental passthrough, never cached.
Done (Sonnet): cause: crates/elab/src/std_dir.rs:179 env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR") (absolute path) is kept unremapped in kache keys, so elab missed in every checkout and driver, lsp, cli and the binary after it (~90 s of each build); deps, core, syntax, rt hit; store 28 GiB, hit rate 88%, not eviction. tickets.body:
[Sonnet] Overmind, 28 Nov: red once at 4cdc0e87e in the loop's niced lsp-features step right after the quick tier (test 13.7 s vs 7 s usually); not reproduced alone 3/3 there nor in the full step 50/50, nor 3/3 on Speedwell. Ladder: crates/driver/src/search_at.rs (RUNG_TIME, LADDER_TIME).

Lane: cause found. The 500 ms rung is not the problem (byComputing checks in 0.00 s). The search's 5 s clock (started + options.time) began before generate_deferred_equations, which takes ~2.4 s on a cold start in this test (lsp session, searcher with no warm equations), ~5 s niced after the quick tier; the ladder checker's deadline was then already past, so the ladder was skipped and the full search ran (left 3, right 1). Not changed: rung wall budgets (a count budget would not have helped).
